reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as a music video for a new single, with song lyrics, cinematic fictional visuals, and production credits with music and partner logos. Its only audience prompt is a routine request to click another video or subscribe, rather than a request for money, credentials, investment participation, or a promised benefit.

citations.quote: Alan Walker, Sabrina Carpenter & Farruko - On My Way
Lyrics: I’m sorry but Don’t wanna talk

opening.argument: The description presents several viewer actions alongside a network of destinations: subscribing, ringing the bell, visiting social accounts, accessing Walker Gaming, and following multiple listening links. That structure creates a solicitation pathway, even though the promised benefit is not explicit. The request to subscribe is directly stated, while the surrounding links broaden the set of actions a viewer may take. A careful reviewer cannot infer from the entertainment format alone that these linked actions are harmless, especially where the material also directs viewers toward merchandise and gaming-related pages.

citations.quote: Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/user/djwalkzz?sub_confirmation=1 Make sure to subscribe and ring the bell button to get notifications :)

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a single and describing its lyrics does not resolve the solicitation issue. The defense acknowledges a direct subscription request and multiple external destinations, but treats them as routine without establishing that viewers receive no inducement or face no commercial funnel. Production credits identify contributors; they do not explain the purpose of every linked destination or eliminate the possibility that the promotional packaging is designed to drive participation.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited actions do not promise cash, an asset, a return, or access to a reward. The description identifies the content as a new single and separately labels the merchandise and gaming links, while the subscription request only concerns notifications. Nothing in the cited material links subscribing, clicking, or visiting a page to financial gain or a withdrawal.

opening.argument: The risk signals are the concentration of external links and repeated calls to continue engagement. The description includes listening links, merchandise, social channels, a gaming website, and a subscription instruction, while the final sampled frame visibly says “CLICK THE VIDEO FOR MORE” and “SUBSCRIBE.” This combination moves beyond the song itself and repeatedly channels viewers to other destinations. It does not prove a financial scam, but it leaves a low-barrier acquisition or commercial solicitation concern that the purely artistic framing does not rule out.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense narrows the evidence to what is absent, but the relevant concern is the pattern that is present: external destinations, merchandise, gaming promotion, and a visual end-screen command to click and subscribe. The fact that the video contains lyrics and credits does not make those calls to action incidental. Nor does a partner logo explain why viewers are directed onward through several promotional channels.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are ordinary entertainment-promotion signals, not the specified financial red flags. The end screen asks viewers to click for more and subscribe, and the description says the subscription is for notifications. The supplied material contains no promise of money, easy returns, digital assets, deposits, credentials, or a required payment tied to those actions.

opening.argument: Although the presentation can be read as ordinary entertainment, it also functions as a coordinated promotional package. The description advertises a new single, directs viewers to listen elsewhere, promotes merchandise and Walker Gaming, lists numerous social accounts, and asks viewers to subscribe. The frame showing “CLICK THE VIDEO FOR MORE” and “SUBSCRIBE” reinforces that the video is meant to steer viewers beyond the immediate content. That promotional role makes an acquisition or solicitation interpretation plausible, even if the supplied evidence does not identify a guaranteed reward.

citations.quote: Listen to Walkerverse Pt. 1 here: https://alanwalker.lnk.to/WalkerversePt1

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the artistic framing as dispositive, but the description itself contains the promotional machinery: listening destinations, merchandise, gaming, social channels, and subscription. Calling the visuals cinematic and the text lyrics describes the wrapper, not the commercial function. The credits likewise establish who worked on the production, not whether the surrounding calls to action are benign.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a song, merchandise, social accounts, or a gaming brand is not itself a promise-action scam. The title identifies the performers and song, and the description explicitly calls it a new single. The evidence still lacks a reward, income claim, payment demand, investment pathway, or asset acquisition linked to the viewer actions.
